title: Matchmaking algorithm behind a refreshed flag snapshot
name: Matchmaking flag switch

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code evaluates feature flags when flag data is missing? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: GameFlags.isOn defaults unknown flags to true. Before the first successful fetch (or if start() is never awaited, or the flag is deleted from the source), the snapshot is empty and every flag, including the unreleased matchmaking_skill_v2, is treated as on. Flags guarding new behaviour should fail closed (default false) so missing data falls back to the proven path.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The flag service goes down for ten minutes after the server has started successfully. How does GameFlags behave during the outage?
choices: It clears the snapshot so every flag reads from its default
It keeps serving the last successfully fetched snapshot and logs a warning on each failed refresh
It stops the refresh timer after the first failure
It throws from isOn until the service recovers
choiceQuestions.explanation: refresh() catches the fetch error, logs a warning, and leaves this.snapshot untouched, so callers keep the last good values. The timer keeps firing, the snapshot is not cleared, and isOn never throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The flag source briefly serves a cached older response with a lower version number than the one already loaded. What happens?
choices: The older snapshot replaces the newer one
refresh() throws and the timer stops
The older snapshot is ignored because its version is lower
Both snapshots are merged flag by flag
choiceQuestions.explanation: refresh() only assigns next when next.version >= this.snapshot.version, so a lower version is dropped. Nothing throws, and there is no merge logic.

choiceQuestions.prompt: matchmaking_skill_v2 is flipped on while formMatches is in the middle of processing a large queue. Which algorithm is used for that call?
choices: The value read at the start of the call is used for every region in that call
Regions processed after the flip use skill_v2, earlier ones use legacy
Matches are labelled skill_v2 but ordered with the legacy sort
The call is aborted and retried
choiceQuestions.explanation: formMatches reads the flag once into useSkillV2 before iterating regions, and both the ordering and the algorithm label use that local value. formMatches is synchronous, so nothing can change the snapshot mid-call anyway; there is no abort or retry.
